body:
# Independent audit: affine sampled support and closed normal sectors



Audited source:
affine-sampled-support-normal-sector-zero-incoming-minkowski.md.
The source is a geometric transport theorem, not an OC induction or
a statement that arbitrary minimizing families have affine supports.

## 1. Canonical hull and exact normal-sector identification

The canonical hull is contained in the original convex body and
contains each prescribed fiber. Thus its integer sections equal
the original sections. Its projected integer points are precisely
the same complete base P. This remains valid when the original
body has noninteger padding outside the canonical hull.

For h_p(u)=a.p+b, the functional u.x-a.z is bounded by b on
every generating fiber, hence on the hull. Equality at base p
is precisely the exposed u-face of K_p. For a full-dimensional
polytope, this face either is a facet, whose relative interior
has unique normal u, or has zero own-boundary measure.
Consequently the physical restriction to the supporting face
is exactly the normal-u sector, modulo target-null sets.
Absolute continuity transfers this identity to the source.
For d=1 the identity is exact on the appropriate endpoint,
with counting measure.

Normal preservation therefore prohibits both entering and
leaving this physical face. No claim that arbitrary ambient
facet restrictions automatically have this property is used.
The restricted rows keep the physical martingale condition
and fill the entire restricted target.

## 2. Dimension, lattice, and metric

When P spans R^n, a positive measured face in one fiber supplies
d-1 independent continuous directions, and the projection of
the global supporting face contains P. These directions together
give dimension n+d-1. The canonical hull has dimension n+d, so
the face is a true facet. If P does not span, the source correctly
withholds a full-dimensional reduced body in the original base
coordinates.

The straightening

    Psi(z,t)=(z,Et+(a.z+b)u)

preserves the base coordinate and is an isometry on each fixed
fiber. Thus there is exactly unit Jacobian for the discrete
fiber measure. The separate ambient surface Jacobian is
sqrt(1+|a|^2), because the base-column Gram matrix is I+aa^T
and the continuous columns are orthonormal and orthogonal to
those added u-components. This ambient factor must not enter
the mixed measure, and the source does not insert it.

All exposed fiber faces are nonempty, so the reduced base is
exactly P. Lower-dimensional faces contribute zero, while
positive sector mass gives at least one face of dimension d-1.
The finite disjoint union therefore has intrinsic dimension
d-1 and precisely the claimed Hausdorff fiber-sum measure.
This also treats d=1 as singleton counting measure.

## 3. Global affinity and facet ownership

If every sampled support is affine, any representation of a
real base z gives the same support function for its Minkowski
combination. Every point of the hull is in such a combination,
so all real canonical sections have that support function.

For a nonvertical canonical facet with normal (c,v), each
point maximizes v.x in its own real fiber. With u=v/|v|,
the facet lies in F_u and in the base-only hyperplane

    (c+|v|a(u)).z=beta-|v|b(u).

If its base coefficient were nonzero, these would be two
independent hyperplane conditions, reducing dimension below
n+d-1. Therefore the coefficient is zero and the facet is
F_u. This proof uses the actual real sections just established.

A facet may have zero sampled boundary measure; the source
explicitly permits this. For measured own-boundary points,
the positive normal sector supplies its global facet. Any other
nonvertical facet containing a positive-measure part of the same
own-facet would have the same continuous unit normal, and hence
the same affine supporting plane on spanning P. Thus ownership
is unique almost everywhere in the claimed, nonvertical sense.
Vertical projection facets can also meet boundary-base fibers,
which does not contradict this formulation.

## 4. Source law, caps, and the obstruction to recursion

Substitution into c.z+v.x>=beta gives

    (c+(v.u)a).z+(E^T v).t>=beta-(v.u)b,

with exactly the signs shown in the source. Vanishing continuous
normal, whole-plane traces, and cap-boundary allocations remain
in the formulation. The proof does not identify an arbitrary
positive boundary allocation with a closed-cap indicator when
the entire reduced fiber is on the cap boundary.

In the constant-cube example, the source density
(3/4,3/2,3/4) has total mass three. The middle row sends
(1/4,1,1/4), has total mass 3/2 and mean one; the endpoint
rows remain fixed. Each target base receives one. The two caps
z<=3/2 and z>=1/2, each weighted 3/4, produce exactly this
density and both have original bulk mass two.

The source's z^2 moment is 9/2 and the target's is five.
Thus the inherited volume law is genuinely nonconstant even
though every normal sector is closed. In reduced continuous
dimension at least one, it has positive mass in fiber interiors,
where reduced own-boundary measure is zero. This certifies the
claimed failure to reinterpret it as reduced boundary stress.
For d=1 the reduced object is counting measure, as stated.

No correction is required. The result removes an incoming term
under an exact affine-support hypothesis; it does not identify
the restricted cap budgets with the original bulk budgets or
produce the lower-dimensional optimality conditions needed
for an OC induction.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
